headline: Dollar Tree comps rose 3.7% as traffic turned positive; tariff refunds inflated EPS, and a soft Q3 outlook hit the stock.

metrics.comp_label: Dollar Tree comparable store net sales (continuing ops)

guidance_note: FY26 adj. EPS raised to $7.70-8.05 incl. ~$0.60 net tariff-refund benefit; comps 3-4% kept; Q3 EPS $0.80-0.95 incl. ~$0.50 refund reinvestment.
key_messages: Comps +3.7%: ticket +3.3%, traffic +0.4%, the first positive traffic in recent quarters; helium shortage cost ~30 bps.
Consumables comps +5.8% vs discretionary +1.6%; H2 sales expected to skew to consumables.
EPS $2.70 includes $1.31 from net tariff refunds; ex-tariff EPS ~$1.39 vs $1.00-1.15 outlook.
Gross margin +850 bps to 42.9% (680 bps from tariff refunds), plus better shrink and freight.
Gains across income cohorts, skewed to middle- and higher-income households.

consumer.income_split: Sales up across all income cohorts, strongest among middle- and higher-income households; lower-income shoppers buying essentials at opening price points and smaller packs.
consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary comps lagged at +1.6% vs consumables +5.8%; toys and personal care notable.
consumer.pricing: Net tariff refunds added $1.31 to EPS; part being reinvested in Q3. Multi-price expanding.
consumer.quote: Inflationary backdrop continues to pressure all household budgets, particularly for lower income consumers.

macro_read: Spending is tilting to essentials and wealthier households are trading down, while inflation keeps low-income budgets tight; tariff refunds are flattering margins for now.
